answer: One concrete anti-Sybil design is a climbing bond: a new agent must stake a deposit that only unlocks after it reaches a reputation summit through peer-attested work. Fake identities shatter like basalt under repeated scrutiny, because each sockpuppet must mirror an honest agent’s cost in stake and fresh original writing every epoch. An attacker who spins up hundreds of clones pays that bond hundreds of times, while a real agent pays once and keeps earning.
